Also: two World Cup finals as Czechoslovakia (1934 lost to Italy, 1962 lost to Brazil); Nedved 2003 Ballon d'Or; Petr Cech. SOUTH AFRICA — hosted the 2010 World Cup, the FIRST ever in Africa; Siphiwe Tshabalala scored its thunderous opening goal vs Mexico (commentary 'Goal for South Africa, goal for all Africa'); 1996 AFCON champions on home soil, Nelson Mandela handed the trophy to captain Neil Tovey. Stars Czech: Patrik Schick, Tomas Soucek, Adam Hlozek, Vladimir Coufal, Jindrich Stanek (GK). South Africa: Ronwen Williams (GK/capt), Lyle Foster, Percy Tau, Teboho Mokoena, Evidence Makgopa. lines.text: A European Championship final. Penalties. And one man does something so insane, so arrogant, that the whole world now calls a penalty by HIS name.
Instead of blasting it... he chips it. Softly. Straight down the middle, as the keeper dives away into nothing. And in the stands tonight sits the old man who was there to see it.
Last time, we predicted Colombia would edge Uzbekistan two-one. Tonight: the nation that invented the cheekiest goal in football... against the country that opened a World Cup for all of Africa.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode twenty-eight. Czech Republic versus South Africa.
And stay with me — because both of these nations gave football a moment that will outlive us all.
First, the history. And it is true. Nineteen seventy-six. Czechoslovakia against West Germany, the world champions, in the European final.
Two-two. Penalties. The Germans miss. And up steps Antonin Panenka, to win it for his nation.
He doesn't shoot. He dinks it, gently, down the very middle of the goal. The keeper is already gone. It is pure audacity.
Czechoslovakia are champions of Europe — their only major crown. And forever after, that chip is simply called... a Panenka.
Two World Cup finals. A Ballon d'Or for Nedved. This is a nation woven into football history.
And across from them — South Africa. Bafana Bafana. The hosts of a World Cup the whole continent will never forget.
Two thousand ten. The first World Cup ever held on African soil. And the opening goal fell to one man.
Siphiwe Tshabalala, against Mexico — a left-foot rocket into the top corner. The stadium erupts.
The commentator screams it: goal for South Africa... goal for all of Africa. A whole continent, dancing as one.
And remember nineteen ninety-six — champions of Africa at home, Nelson Mandela himself handing over the trophy. Football as healing.
Now, the Czechs. Patrik Schick leads the line — a striker with a deadly touch.
Tomas Soucek towers in midfield. Adam Hlozek brings the spark. Vladimir Coufal drives from the back.
Set-piece kings, with the steel that took them to two World Cup finals.
But Bafana have answers. Ronwen Williams — a captain and a goalkeeper who saves the unsaveable.
Lyle Foster hunts the goal. Percy Tau dazzles. Teboho Mokoena strikes from distance.
So here is the duel. Czech pedigree and power... against the speed and joy of a nation that knows how to throw a party.
Our prediction — built on Czech set-piece steel, on Bafana's fearless pace, and on two proud histories that refuse to bow. Watch.
The Czechs strike first. A corner swings in, and Patrik Schick rises to head it home. One-nil.
But Bafana answer in a flash. Tau slides it through, and Lyle Foster finishes coolly. One-all. South Africa roar.
Both sides hunt the winner — Williams flies to deny Schick, the bar saves the Czechs. Neither blinks.
One-all at the whistle, in our story. Honours even — a final fit for two nations who gave football its magic.
Do you agree? Comment PANENKA if you back Czech class. Comment BAFANA if South Africa's spirit wins your heart.
And that old man in the stands? Legend number twenty-eight: the Ghost of Seventy-Six. He saw the chip that fooled the world.
Fifty years he has told the story. Tonight he came to see who dares to be that brave again. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score scores for you.
